questions.stem: The acronym GSM stands for
questions.explanation: GSM is the Global System for Mobile Communications standard used by Nigerian networks.

questions.stem: Diverting incoming calls to another number when a subscriber is busy or unreachable is called
questions.explanation: Call forwarding (divert) redirects calls; call barring blocks selected incoming or outgoing calls.

questions.stem: A message that carries pictures, audio or video clips between phones is sent by
questions.explanation: MMS (Multimedia Messaging Service) carries media; SMS carries short text only; IMEI is the handset identity number.

questions.topic: Mobile Phone Bands and Their Uses
questions.stem: A quad-band GSM phone is useful to a traveller because it
options: can operate on the 850, 900, 1800 and 1900 MHz bands used in different countries
can hold four SIM cards at once
questions.explanation: Different regions use different GSM bands; a quad-band handset covers all four main ones.

questions.stem: A phone whose two halves are hinged so that it opens like a clam shell is a
questions.explanation: Flip (clamshell) phones fold on a hinge; their flex cable through the hinge needs special care.

questions.stem: The flex (ribbon) cable of a flip or slide phone needs special attention during maintenance mainly because
options: repeated opening and closing bends it and causes cracks and display faults
it carries the high-voltage antenna signal
it is soldered to the SIM card
questions.explanation: Constant flexing fatigues the cable, a common cause of display or keypad failure in folding phones.

questions.stem: The accessory that allows a phone user to make calls without holding the phone, through a wire or Bluetooth link, is the
questions.explanation: A headset/hands-free kit provides microphone and earpiece away from the handset.

questions.stem: The menu used to store names and telephone numbers on a phone is the
questions.explanation: Contacts (phone book) stores names and numbers; settings changes how the phone works.

questions.stem: The government agency that regulates mobile network operators such as MTN, Airtel, Glo and 9mobile in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: The NCC licenses and regulates telecommunications operators in Nigeria.

questions.stem: The national emergency telephone number that can be dialled free from any network in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: Nigeria uses 112 as its toll-free national emergency number.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of computer SOFTWARE?
questions.explanation: Software is a set of programs, such as the operating system; keyboard and monitor are hardware.

questions.stem: A computer is needed in a phone repair workshop mainly to
options: solder components on the circuit board
run flashing and diagnostic software connected to the phone
questions.explanation: Flashing and diagnostic tools run on a PC connected to the phone by cable or box; soldering and heating need other tools.

questions.stem: Arrange the following mobile data technologies from SLOWEST to FASTEST.
questions.explanation: GPRS (2.5G) is slowest, EDGE (2.75G) improves on it, and 3G is faster still.

questions.stem: Copying a file from a website on the internet onto a phone's memory is called
questions.explanation: Downloading receives data from the internet; uploading sends data to it.

questions.stem: In the basic block diagram of a mobile phone, the block that transmits and receives radio signals through the antenna is the
questions.explanation: The radio unit contains the transceiver and power amplifier; the power unit manages battery supply.

questions.stem: The component in a phone that produces silent alerts by shaking the handset is the
questions.explanation: A small motor with an off-centre weight produces vibration; the buzzer produces sound.

questions.stem: The part of a phone that holds the subscriber identity module and connects it to the circuit board is the
questions.explanation: The SIM socket contacts connect the SIM chip to the phone; dirty or bent contacts cause "insert SIM" errors.

questions.stem: Android and iOS are examples of mobile phone
options: hardware drivers on the SIM card
questions.explanation: They are operating systems that manage the hardware and run applications.

questions.stem: On a phone circuit board, a tiny two-terminal component marked with a stripe at one end, used to allow current in one direction, is a
questions.explanation: The stripe (band) marks the cathode of a diode; resistors and most SMD capacitors have no polarity mark.

questions.stem: The large IC that controls the battery charging, voltage regulation and power distribution in a smartphone is the
questions.explanation: The PMIC manages supplies; faults in it often cause no-power or charging problems.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of PREVENTIVE maintenance of a mobile phone?
options: Cleaning dust from the charging port before it causes a fault
Flashing a phone that will not boot
questions.explanation: Preventive maintenance is done before a fault occurs; the others repair existing faults.

questions.stem: Removing a BGA chip, cleaning its pads and re-applying solder balls with a stencil before refitting it is called
questions.explanation: Re-balling restores the solder ball array of BGA chips, usually with a stencil and hot air.

questions.topic: Common Tools and Equipment for Hardware and Software Repairs
questions.stem: The tool used to remove and refit small surface-mount components using a stream of heated air is the
questions.explanation: Hot-air stations melt solder around SMD components; multimeters and oscilloscopes only measure.

questions.topic: Common Tools and Equipment for Hardware and Software Repairs
questions.stem: A regulated d.c. power supply with an ammeter is useful in phone repair because it
options: shows the current the board draws when powered, helping to locate shorts and dead faults
questions.explanation: Abnormal current readings point to short circuits or dead sections of the board.

questions.stem: A phone technician wears an anti-static wrist strap connected to earth mainly to
options: prevent electrostatic discharge from damaging sensitive ICs
questions.explanation: Static charge on the body can destroy CMOS chips; the strap drains it to earth safely through a high resistance.

questions.stem: Which safety facility must be provided in every phone repair workshop?
options: First aid box and fire extinguisher
questions.explanation: First aid and fire-fighting equipment are basic workshop safety requirements.

questions.stem: A phone charges only when the cable is held at a particular angle. The most likely fault is
options: a loose or worn charging port
questions.explanation: Intermittent contact depending on cable position indicates a worn or poorly soldered charging port.

questions.stem: A phone bought abroad displays "SIM not supported" with a Nigerian SIM but works with its original network's SIM. The phone is most likely
options: network locked to the original operator
in need of a new battery
questions.explanation: A network (carrier) lock restricts the phone to one operator's SIMs; the hardware is otherwise working.

questions.stem: The first step in troubleshooting a phone brought in as "dead" is to
options: check the battery and charging system with a known-good battery or power supply
questions.explanation: Start with simple, likely causes; a flat or faulty battery is the most common reason for a dead phone.

questions.topic: Tracing and Fault Finding in Hardware
questions.stem: With the battery removed, a technician measures 0.2 ohms between the battery positive (VBAT) line and ground on the phone board. This indicates
options: an open circuit in the VBAT line
a short circuit on the VBAT line, often a shorted capacitor or IC
questions.explanation: A near-zero reading between supply and ground shows a short; components on that line are then checked, e.g. by injecting a small voltage and feeling for heat.

questions.topic: Tracing and Fault Finding in Hardware
questions.stem: A continuity test with a multimeter is used to check whether
options: a conductor or track forms a complete path with very low resistance
the software is up to date
questions.explanation: Continuity mode beeps when the resistance is very low, showing a complete path; a broken track gives no beep.

questions.stem: Re-installing the firmware (operating software) of a phone using a computer and suitable software is called
questions.explanation: Flashing writes new firmware into the phone's flash memory, curing boot loops and corrupted software.

questions.stem: Before flashing a customer's phone, the technician should first
options: back up the user's data where possible and confirm the correct firmware for the exact model
questions.explanation: Flashing may erase data and the wrong firmware can damage the phone; changing an IMEI is illegal.

questions.topic: Setting up a Mobile Phone Workshop
questions.stem: Which factor is MOST important when choosing a location for a phone repair shop?
options: Nearness to customers in a busy commercial area
questions.explanation: Customers must find and reach the shop easily; busy commercial areas give more patronage.

questions.topic: Facilities and Equipment for Mobile Phone Workshop
questions.stem: An ultrasonic cleaner is used in a phone workshop to
options: remove corrosion and dirt from water-damaged circuit boards
questions.explanation: Ultrasonic waves in isopropyl alcohol or cleaning fluid dislodge corrosion from under components.

questions.stem: A technician buys a replacement screen for ₦18,500, sets labour at ₦6,000 and allows ₦1,500 for overheads (power, rent share). What should the customer be charged?
questions.explanation: Charge = parts + labour + overheads = 18,500 + 6,000 + 1,500 = ₦26,000.

questions.stem: A phone repair business was set up with ₦1,200,000 and made a net profit of ₦300,000 in its first year. The return on investment is
questions.explanation: ROI = net profit / investment x 100 = 300,000 / 1,200,000 x 100 = 25%.

questions.stem: A replacement phone battery is rated 4500 mAh. If the phone draws an average of 250 mA, about how long will a full charge last?
questions.explanation: Time = capacity / current = 4500 mAh / 250 mA = 18 hours (ideal).

questions.stem: A customer brings in a phone that fell into a bucket of water ten minutes ago. Which action should the technician take FIRST?
options: Switch it on to test whether it still works
Disconnect the battery, open the phone and clean the board with isopropyl alcohol before any power is applied
Plug it into a charger to dry it out
Heat the whole phone in an oven
questions.explanation: Applying power to a wet board causes short circuits and rapid corrosion; disconnecting power and cleaning with isopropyl alcohol gives the best chance of recovery.

questions.stem: During calls, the user hears the other person clearly but the other person cannot hear the user. The component MOST likely to be faulty is the
questions.explanation: Outgoing voice is picked up by the microphone; the earpiece reproduces incoming voice, which is working.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the three main blocks in the basic block diagram of a mobile phone. [3 marks]
(b) State one function of each block named in (a). [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) 1 mark each: power unit (battery, charging and power management); memory unit (storage and processing/logic); radio (RF) unit (transmitter/receiver and antenna)
3 marks: (b) 1 mark each: power unit - supplies and regulates voltages to all sections and controls charging; memory unit - stores operating software, user data and instructions for the processor; radio unit - transmits and receives signals between phone and base station
questions.explanation: Power unit: supplies and regulates power and charging. Memory unit: stores software and data used by the processor. Radio unit: transmits and receives RF signals through the antenna.

questions.stem:
(a) Define preventive maintenance. [2 marks]
(b) State four advantages of preventive maintenance of mobile phones. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Routine care carried out on a phone before faults occur, e.g. cleaning and inspection, to keep it working and prevent breakdown
4 marks: (b) Any four, 1 mark each: prevents sudden breakdown; extends the life of the phone; reduces repair cost; detects faults early; keeps performance high; protects user data
questions.explanation: Preventive maintenance is planned care done before faults occur. It prevents breakdowns, extends life, lowers cost, finds faults early and keeps the phone performing well.

questions.topic: Common Tools and Equipment for Hardware and Software Repairs
questions.stem: State the use of each of the following in a phone repair workshop: (a) soldering iron (b) desoldering pump (sucker) (c) multimeter (d) precision screwdriver set (e) flashing software (f) magnifying lamp or microscope. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Soldering iron: melts solder to join components and wires to the board
1 mark: (b) Desoldering pump: sucks molten solder away to remove components
1 mark: (c) Multimeter: measures voltage, current, resistance and tests continuity of components
1 mark: (d) Precision screwdriver set: opens and assembles phones with tiny screws (star/Torx, Phillips etc.)
1 mark: (e) Flashing software: installs or reinstalls the phone's firmware/operating system
1 mark: (f) Magnifier/microscope: enlarges small SMD components and solder joints for inspection and repair
questions.explanation: Soldering iron joins; sucker removes solder; multimeter measures and tests; precision screwdrivers open the phone; flashing software reinstalls firmware; magnifier aids inspection of tiny parts.

questions.stem:
(a) State three common software problems of mobile phones. [3 marks]
(b) Explain three possible causes of the message "SIM card rejected" or "Invalid SIM". [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) Any three, 1 mark each: phone hanging/freezing; restarting (boot loop); "contact service provider"; phone lock code forgotten; "SIM card rejected"/"invalid SIM"; apps crashing; corrupted firmware
3 marks: (b) Any three, 1 mark each: phone network-locked to another operator; damaged or deactivated/unregistered SIM; corrupted firmware or invalid IMEI; dirty or faulty SIM socket
questions.explanation: Software problems include freezing, boot loops, network lock messages, forgotten lock codes and SIM errors. "SIM rejected/invalid" can be due to network lock, a damaged or deactivated SIM, corrupted firmware/IMEI, or a dirty SIM socket.

questions.topic: Tracing and Fault Finding in Hardware
questions.stem: Describe how a technician would trace the fault in a phone that does not power on, using visual inspection and metering methods. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Visual inspection under magnification for corrosion, burnt or missing components, cracked solder or physical damage
1 mark: Test the battery voltage with a multimeter or try a known-good battery
1 mark: Connect a regulated d.c. power supply and observe current draw when the power key is pressed
1 mark: Measure resistance between VBAT and ground to check for a short circuit
1 mark: Check the power key switch and track continuity to the PMIC
1 mark: Measure output voltages of the power management IC/regulators and compare with specification; replace/re-ball faulty component
questions.explanation: Inspect visually for damage and corrosion, test the battery, power the board from a d.c. supply and watch the current, check VBAT for shorts, test the power switch and its tracks, then measure regulator/PMIC outputs against specification and replace the faulty part.

questions.topic: Setting up a Mobile Phone Workshop
questions.stem:
(a) State three factors to consider when choosing a location for a mobile phone workshop. [3 marks]
(b) List three items of equipment needed to set up the workshop. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) Any three, 1 mark each: nearness to customers/market; security; steady power supply; accessibility; cost of rent; competition; availability of spare parts suppliers
3 marks: (b) Any three, 1 mark each: soldering station; hot-air rework station; multimeter; regulated d.c. power supply; computer with flashing software; ultrasonic cleaner; microscope/magnifier; ESD mat and wrist strap
questions.explanation: Location: customers, security, power, access, rent, competition, parts supply. Equipment: soldering and hot-air stations, multimeter, d.c. supply, computer and software, ultrasonic cleaner, magnifier, ESD protection.
